Summary (full text)

Camera secuplug-t10-jxh42 (T10) in the light box with the SpyderCheckr 24 chart, lamps 3000 K. Both stacks ran on the same camera, the same chart position and the same light: the open stack (open-tx-isp + OpenIMP + timps) and the vendor stack (Ingenic ISP module + vendor libimp + timps built for it), one after the other.

Result: 62 pass, 4 fail (1 accepted, 3 issues), 111 info/warn, 1 planned checks not run in these runs.

Failed checks: frame luma p1_night (AE target, default comp 128) (open 85.0, vendor 74.8; pass = open within +-10 % of vendor); H.264 CBR 1000: PSNR mean / min (dB) (open 37.74 / 37.12, vendor 39.05 / 37.93; pass = open mean >= vendor - 0.5 dB); H.264 CBR 1000: blocking / ghosting flags (open blk 1.12, blocking (border/inner step +0.12 > 0.10), vendor blk 1.10, none; blk = 8-px border/inner step of the error image (1.00 = none); fail = open flagged and vendor not, warn = both flagged); time to a stable picture: WB preset 1 at 3000 K (s) (open >64, vendor 22; not stable within 60 s; 3 shots 3 s apart within 1 % R/G, B/G and 1 Y).

Warnings: H.264 FixQP 25: blocking / ghosting flags (open blk 1.15, blocking (border/inner step +0.15 > 0.10), vendor blk 1.12, blocking (border/inner step +0.12 > 0.10)): blk = 8-px border/inner step of the error image (1.00 = none); fail = open flagged and vendor not, warn = both flagged; H.264 FixQP 35: blocking / ghosting flags (open blk 1.14, blocking (border/inner step +0.14 > 0.10), vendor blk 1.11, blocking (border/inner step +0.11 > 0.10)): blk = 8-px border/inner step of the error image (1.00 = none); fail = open flagged and vendor not, warn = both flagged; H.264 CBR 2000: blocking / ghosting flags (open blk 1.14, blocking (border/inner step +0.14 > 0.10), vendor blk 1.11, blocking (border/inner step +0.11 > 0.10)): blk = 8-px border/inner step of the error image (1.00 = none); fail = open flagged and vendor not, warn = both flagged; picture check before d1d4 (open picture not intact , vendor picture not intact; colour cast red ): advisory (Claude vision, lamps_off); see vision/d1d4.json; advisory (Claude vision, lamps_off); see vision/d1d4.json.

Passed: frame luma p1_day (AE target, default comp 128); chart grey RG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); chart grey BG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); p1_day dE00 mean, unclipped patches; p1_day dE00 mean, grey-normalised; grey row tone slope; MTF50 median of 8 chart edges (cycles/pixel); 10-90 % edge rise median (px); H.264 FixQP 25: decodes clean; H.264 FixQP 25: PSNR mean vs reference (dB); ...

How to read: "pass" means the open stack is equal to or better than the vendor stack within the tolerance named in each row; matched-exposure rows (A2) compare the same integration time and gain on both stacks, read back from the ISP.

A5 Encoder (H.264): open vs vendor, same settings

Cells = open / vendor. Static chart scene, lamps on, day pinned, streamer restarted per case with a /tmp conf. Bytes per frame and P/I from ffprobe -show_frames (frames before the first IDR and, for CBR, the first seconds are ignored). PSNR / SSIM (luma) of every decoded frame (SSIM every 2th) against the mean image of the stack's own H.264 FixQP reference recording, so the ISP difference between the stacks drops out; sensor noise stays in (see the noise-floor row): an encoder that smooths noise can score higher than the reference. blk = blockiness of the error image (step across 8-px borders / step inside, 1.00 = no block structure); GOP drift = PSNR of the IDR minus the last P of the GOP. n/a = the streamer of that stack did not take the setting.

run-t10-1110-fulllogsopenflagNo oops, BUG, I2C or reset failures: reload cycles 6-10 all passed (sensor bound and released correctly, oops=0), and the day/night D1/D4 transitions passed. The main concerns are the excessive repeated T20FW switch_wdr/mesh_reload bursts with occasional ms-scale stalls, a vision-flagged black/banded picture with wrong IR mode before d1d4, an invalid AE settle measurement, and inconsistent day/night start-up latency.
anomalies: T20FW firmware repeats the switch_wdr/mesh_reload sequence many times in bursts within a few milliseconds. This happens about 4x at 3455.36 and about 8x at 3476.75 in reload 8, and 4x at 3493.24 and about 8x at 3514.63 in reload 9. The same WDR/mesh tables are reloaded with mode=0 unchanged each time, which suggests redundant or looping reloads in the ISP driver or firmware., Occasional latency spikes inside the WDR table loads, for example table6 at 3514.627652 -> 3514.636000 (~8 ms) and lut11 at 3514.639867 -> 3514.644926 (~5 ms), against the normal ~70 us., Firmware LUT/mesh buffer addresses differ between reloads (c104e000 in reload 8 vs c113a000 in reload 9). This is expected after a module reload, but worth checking for a memory leak across rmmod/insmod cycles., The pre-d1d4 vision check failed: picture nearly black and noise-only, with horizontal banding/stripe noise. Night/IR mode looked inactive (colour noise instead of monochrome), even though AE had been re-pinned to day mode (exposure 20684) with the lamps off. This may be an ISP mode or banding issue after the forced-night/pin_day transition., The aeresp lamps-off settle result was INVALID: no settle point within the clip window (21.16 s, overshoot 116.8 %, Y 86.2 -> 5.3, peak deviation 1249 %). This is mostly a test-window issue, but the AE trace shows Iridix still changing late (17 changes)., Day/night detection in the second streamer session took about 40 s for the first look versus about 5 s in the previous session, an inconsistent daynight start-up latency.; severity: medium
run-t10-1110-fulllogsvendorflagThe camera produced no snapshots for the whole run, so all 16 test phases were skipped even though the streamer reported 'up' and was restarted before each phase. This persistent capture failure points to a likely ISP driver (tx_isp_t10), sensor (jxh42) or libimp firmware hang. Recovery required a sysrq reboot, and no kernel logs were captured to confirm the root cause.
anomalies: Every phase preflight failed with no snapshot (0/0 bytes): noisecurve, mtf, sub, flicker, ssim, rc, enc, startup, cpu, api, stab, reload, motion, aeresp, nightir, d1d4. All 16 phases were not measured., The streamer (timpsd, libimp da38e940) reports 'up' after each restart, but it never delivers a frame. This points to a stalled ISP/sensor pipeline (tx_isp_t10 / sensor_jxh42_t10) or a firmware/libimp capture failure, not a userspace crash., A streamer restart (new PIDs 30382 through 32724) never recovered capture. The fault persists across process restarts, which suggests stuck kernel driver or hardware state., Streamer startup info is empty ('timpsd up ( )'). Sensor or mode details may not have been detected or reported., A forced sysrq reboot was needed to restore the camera, and the SSH connection was reset. After reboot, tx_isp_t10 is loaded with 6 users (sensor_jxh42_t10), but there is no post-reboot snapshot check., No kernel dmesg or oops output was captured. The root cause of the frame-delivery failure cannot be confirmed from these logs.; severity: critical

run-t10-1110-vendorlogsvendorflagNo kernel oops, warnings or driver timeouts appear; RTSP stability, snapshots, streamer restarts and the reboot recovery all passed. The main problems are on the ISP/AE side. AE converges very slowly in the dark (about 21-23 s, about 200 % overshoot, so the result was INVALID) and keeps adjusting after lamps on. After the forced night IR phase the image was nearly black, red-tinted and banded, with night mode not active. That points to a day/night or IR-cut state transition problem in the vendor ISP firmware or libimp.
anomalies: aeresp lamps-off step returned INVALID: the settle point fell 0.1 s before the clip end, so the clip window was too short. AE took about 21-23.5 s to settle, overshoot was 203.7 % and peak deviation 295 %. Exposure went from 976.5 to 117007 and Y from 91.3 to 5.3. This means very slow AE convergence on a dark scene., Lamps-on AE shows 128 exposure changes after it got within 5 % of the final value, which suggests AE hunting or oscillation., Exposure did not hold after night IR: the pin_day AE took 30 s to stabilise (exposure 20684 -> 27425) after the phase, versus 9-11 s elsewhere., Vision check before d1d4 flagged the picture as not intact: nearly black, noise only, red/brown colour cast, horizontal banding stripes, and IR night mode not active (colour noise instead of monochrome). The ISP apparently did not stay in night mode, or IR-cut/IR LED control was not restored after the forced night test., Night IR NV12 frames show U/V at exactly 0.000 (perframeUV 128/128). This is expected for monochrome night but is noted., Restore used a sysrq reboot; the SSH connection reset is expected and the camera came back after about 1 min. Not a fault on its own.; severity: medium
run-t10-1110-vendortriagebothinfoBoth fails are on the vendor stack, so they are references, not our defects. Both occurred after a restart and show decode errors; ref_qp10 also shows GOP drift. This points to possible restart or bitstream-capture handling in the setup, or a vendor quirk. Rerun the vendor reference with a warm-up period after restart and verify the decoder before comparing it with the open-source stack.
vendor h264 ref_qp10: unclear (Vendor reference fail: 10 decode errors plus 5.2 dB GOP drift right after a restart could be a vendor encoder issue or a capture/restart artifact; not our defect, so recheck the decode path and restart handling.) | vendor h264 ref_end: unclear (Vendor reference fail: 4 decode errors after a restart with otherwise good PSNR/SSIM suggest a transient stream or decode issue rather than an encoder defect; not ours.)
run-t10-1110-5000logsopenflagNo kernel oops, warnings, timeouts or resets appear, and the module reload during restore completed normally. Concerns are at ISP/firmware level. The lamps-off AE response is invalid because the recording window was too short, and the dark trace shows a very large exposure swing. AE adjusts many times after settling, which suggests hunting. Several WB presets give extreme or duplicate gains (1, 4, 5/6). These may be firmware calibration issues rather than driver faults. A kernel log should be checked to confirm.
anomalies: aeresp lamps-off result INVALID: clip window too short (settle point 0.0 s before clip end, settled in window False). Exposure did not settle within the recording, so AE convergence in the dark is unverified. Overshoot was 156.8 % and peak deviation 845 %. This is most likely a test-harness timing limit, not a confirmed driver fault., AE lamps-off trace: exposure jumped 806.84 -> 117007.03 (about 145x) and Iridix changed 17 times, the last at 2.57 s. This suggests oscillating or hunting dark AE/Iridix control., AE lamps-on: 60 AE changes after reaching within 5 % of final. Method

  • Same camera, same chart position, same lamps; open stack first, then the vendor ISP module + vendor libimp are loaded from /tmp (nothing flashed); the camera returns to the flashed image at the end (module reload or reboot).
  • P1 = camera defaults (AE, AWB, comp 128). P2 = matched exposure: the same integration time and gains on both stacks, set inside the streamer and read back from the ISP; rows whose read-back differs are marked verify=FAIL and not compared.
  • A/A: point p2_a is measured twice (p2_a, p2_a2); the relative difference is the repeatability of the method. A difference between the stacks counts only beyond 2 x that spread (floor 5 %).
  • NV12 noise is measured on raw NV12 frames from the streamer (no JPEG in the path): temporal standard deviation per pixel over the burst, mean over Y 32..224, and U/V.
  • Colour: SpyderCheckr 24 detected automatically, sRGB -> Lab (D50), CIEDE2000 against the Datacolor default values (D50 assumed, not batch specific); 'grey-normalised' removes the white-balance cast first.
  • Sharpness: slanted-edge method on the chart's outer patch edges, frames averaged against noise; JPEG snapshot path.
  • SSIM/PSNR (when run): both stacks record the same static chart scene at the same bitrate; each stream is decoded and compared against a high-bitrate capture of the SAME stack (reference), so the number is the encoder loss of that stack; a cross-stack comparison on static frames is listed separately and includes the ISP difference.
  • Encoder (A5): both stacks get the same timps settings (codec, rc_mode, qp / bitrate, gop) through a /tmp conf and a streamer restart; the recordings come over RTSP (ffmpeg -c copy). The reference is a mean image, because single NV12 frames are not frame-aligned with the stream; the scene is static, so every decoded frame can be compared with it. A second reference at the end of the phase shows whether the scene or the AE moved in between.
  • Lamp switches are made by a person on a marker (NEED_* file); the times above are the marker times.
